user.title: Set up room temperature control
user.description: Choose the existing Hive heating zone and the temperature sensors for each floor. No additional Hive login is needed. An example daily schedule is created: 06:30 downstairs 20°C, 08:30 downstairs 17°C, 17:00 downstairs 20.5°C, and 22:00 upstairs 18°C. Change it afterwards in Configure → Schedule. The thermostat starts Off; confirm the desired Hive fallback before selecting Auto. Leave the optional report-timestamp mapping empty unless your sensor integration exposes actual device report timestamps. After checking a latched fault, use Off → Reset heating fault → Auto/Heat.

init.title: Hive Virtual Thermostat settings
init.description: Changes apply to the running thermostat without switching it Off. Fault latches and request cooldowns are retained. A full Home Assistant restart still starts Off.

sensors.title: Temperature sensors
sensors.description: Choose at least one temperature sensor for each floor. Existing average sensors can be selected if they have the temperature device class. Leave the optional report-timestamp mapping empty unless your sensor integration exposes actual device report timestamps. After checking a latched fault, use Off → Reset heating fault → Auto/Heat.

schedule.title: Weekly temperature schedule
schedule.description: Add, edit or delete a period. Each period applies from its start time until the next matching period. Times use Home Assistant’s local timezone.

add_period.title: Add a schedule period
add_period.description: Choose a time, target, temperature area and days. Avoid a start time already used on the same days.

edit_period.title: Choose a period to edit
edit_period.description: Select the period you want to change.

period.title: Edit schedule period
period.description: Change the time, target, temperature area or days.

delete_period.title: Delete a schedule period
delete_period.description: Select the period to remove. Deleting the final period disables Auto until you add a new period.

safety.title: Safety limits and heating requests
safety.description: Controller requests are timed boosts and expire through Hive. Existing boosts are never cancelled, even after a sensor fault. Test expiry with Home Assistant offline before relying on it. Enable Keep Hive’s own mode and target to manage the fallback in Hive. The fixed fallback field is ignored when enabled. Hive can heat on its own between boosts, even with the virtual thermostat Off or a sensor fault. For sensors that report only on change, availability mode accepts unchanged readings until Home Assistant marks the entity unknown or unavailable. Explicit device-report timestamps still use the timeout. Enable Use remaining sensors when some are unavailable to keep using an area while at least one sensor is available.

schedule_source.title: Schedule source
schedule_source.description: For graphical weekly editing, create a Schedule helper under Settings → Devices & services → Helpers, then select it here. Each block needs Additional data: temperature (°C) and area (Upstairs or Downstairs). Gaps block new heat requests. Disable the helper option to use the built-in weekly periods.
